record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: One part of Nevanlinna theory is devoted to the following problem. How does the geometric structure of a simply connected Riemann covering surface of the sphere influence the value distribution of the meromorphic function generating the surface? It is suggested that one also consider halfsheets among the constituent pieces of such surfaces, which have an infinite number of branch points on their boundary. A typical example is the covering surface generated by ez − z. It contains a right half-plane with a second order branch point at 2πin for each integer n. (F. Huckeman)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In classical Nevanlinna–Ahlfors theory, a non-constant meromorphic function f on the complex plane is represented geometrically by its Riemann covering surface F over the Riemann sphere: F is the simply connected surface obtained by analytic continuation of f^{-1}, and the value distribution of f (deficiencies, ramification, etc.) is reflected in the geometric structure of F. The surface F is built up from "sheets" and "halfsheets" together with branch points; here a halfsheet is a simply connected piece of F lying over a half of the sphere whose boundary may contain infinitely many branch points. A typical example is the surface generated by f(z) = e^{z} − z, which contains a right halfplane in which, for each integer n, there is a branch point of second order over the image of 2πin.

Problem. Develop a value-distribution theory for meromorphic functions whose Riemann covering surfaces of the sphere contain halfsheets with infinitely many branch points on their boundary. Specifically:

(a) Give a precise combinatorial/topological description of admissible halfsheets H, including the distribution (order and accumulation) of branch points on ∂H, that can occur as constituent pieces of the simply connected Riemann covering surface of a meromorphic function on C.

(b) Determine how the presence and structure of such halfsheets in the covering surface F of a meromorphic function f influence the value distribution of f, in particular the Nevanlinna deficiencies δ(a, f), the ramification indices ϑ(a, f), the order and lower order of f, and the deficient/ramified value sets.

(c) Establish quantitative inequalities (analogues of the Second Main Theorem and the defect relation) that incorporate halfsheet contributions, and exhibit a class of explicit examples (beyond e^{z} − z) realizing the prescribed halfsheet structures.
artifact.status_search_result: The proposal, attributed to F. Huckemann, is a programmatic suggestion to extend the classical theory of Riemann covering surfaces (Nevanlinna–Ahlfors) to include halfsheets with infinitely many boundary branch points. While there is continuing research on covering surfaces and branch-point movement in Ahlfors theory (e.g., recent work on movement of branch points in Ahlfors' theory of covering surfaces), no specific resolution of this open-ended program could be located, and no source identifies the suggestion as solved.

status_evidence.title: Movement of branch points in Ahlfors' theory of covering surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper on Ahlfors' theory of covering surfaces, indicating ongoing activity on related questions about branch points in covering surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Research on covering surfaces and branch points in Ahlfors theory continues, but no resolution of Huckemann's specific halfsheet program is identified.

status_evidence.title: Ahlfors' contribution to the theory of meromorphic functions (Eremenko)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing Huckemann among contributors to the theory of meromorphic functions and covering surfaces; no claim that the halfsheet program is settled.
status_evidence.claim: Survey literature on covering-surface theory does not record this proposal as solved.
